official.application_cycle: 2026-2027 PAEC cycle; dLab Global online course runs 16 March - 22 June 2027; results published at www.oas.org/scholarships by February 2027
official.status_note: The OAS Scholarships index lists this announcement under '2026 OPEN ANNOUNCEMENTS' with the deadline 'New Deadline: January 31, 2027', and the GS/OAS online application form for this award (OAS-Universidad del Desarrollo, id 1155) is live.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The announcement states: 'The GS/OAS and the University shall contribute USD 3,400 of the total course fee per selected candidate' and 'The selected candidates will be responsible for USD 400 to cover the remaining cost of the course fee'. Of the USD 3,800 total course fee, USD 3,400 is contributed jointly and the 'remaining course fee of USD 400' is listed under 'EXPENSES NOT COVERED BY THIS SCHOLARSHIP'.
official.funding_period: one-off contribution to the course fee
benefits: The GS/OAS and the University shall contribute USD 3,400 of the total course fee per selected candidate.
The course will be delivered 100% online via a world class Learning Management System - Canvas, used by some of the world's top universities.
All students who successfully complete the program will receive a formal certificate issued by the Universidad del Desarrollo.
During the course we will also be inviting experts in innovation to speak about their projects, as well as connecting you with the innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem at UDD and in Chile.
eligibility: Be a citizen or permanent resident of an OAS member state, except Chile.

Have a strong interest in innovation and entrepreneurship; innovative resilience building business concepts closely linked to climate or environmental resilience, or one that addresses a need in the market, are especially encouraged.
Be a young professional who has an idea to develop, or is in the process of developing a small or medium enterprise in an active OAS member state, and have a strong background in business management.

Be proficient in English; commit to at least 4.5 hours a week to the course over a one-semester period consisting of synchronous (live) and asynchronous content; have access to a computer with a reliable Internet connection with appropriate video and audio functions.
Commit to covering the remaining course fee of USD 400 to the UDD.

The following applicants are not eligible: current OAS scholarship recipients, GS/OAS staff and their immediate family members or GS/OAS consultants, and permanent OAS staff members and their immediate family members.
requirements: Submit a complete application through the online application link; applications with incomplete documentation will not be accepted.
Commit to covering the remaining course fee of USD 400 to the UDD.

The scholarship will be formally awarded only after the selected recipients have signed an OAS Acceptance Form, in which the recipients formally accept the scholarship and agree to its terms and conditions.
Refrain from engaging in activities that are incompatible with their status as an OAS scholarship recipient, in accordance with the rules set forth in the Acceptance Form.
Comply with all academic guidelines requested by UDD and submit any updates to those guidelines and requirements made by the academic authorities of the UDD.
Declining the scholarship after the program start date without proof of force majeure may require the recipient to repay all funds awarded.
documents: Government-issued identification: a copy of either the passport ID page or the national ID card.
Business Concept Statement: a one-paragraph description of an innovative and resilient building business concept that addresses an identified problem or market need.

Curriculum Vitae (CV) or resume, updated, detailing educational background and professional experience, including relevant professional training, certificates and awards in innovation and entrepreneurship if available.

Proof of English proficiency (if applicable): an official transcript confirming completion of studies at an English-speaking university or college within the past five years; or TOEFL 570 or higher (paper-based), 230 or higher (computer-based) or 79 or higher (internet-based/IBT); or an IELTS score of 6.5 or equivalent.

Proof of additional funds (USD 400): proof of property ownership (rental agreement); a bank statement or official bank letter; an employer letter confirming salary during study leave with pay; or a letter confirming a student loan, grant, financial aid or additional scholarship.
selection_criteria: Profile, including education, project outline, recommendation.
Applicant's potential impact on the completion of the course.

A scholarship selection committee pre-selects participants on that profile; pre-selected participants will be contacted via email to participate in an interview with the selection committee, if necessary, in English.
coverage: USD 3,400 of the total course fee of USD 3,800 per selected candidate (final student cost USD 400).
Access to the 100% online course delivered through UDD's Canvas learning management system.
A formal certificate issued by the Universidad del Desarrollo on successful completion of the program.
Connection with the innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem at UDD and in Chile, including invited experts in innovation.
application_method: Combine all required documents into one (1) single PDF file, not exceeding 5 MB, in English or accompanied by an official English translation.
Complete the OAS online scholarship application through the GS/OAS DHDEE application link - only one document upload is permitted by the application system.
Submit the complete application package with all supporting documents to the OAS no later than January 31, 2027.
If pre-selected, respond to the email contact and take part in an interview with the scholarship selection committee in English, if necessary.
If finally selected, sign the formal OAS acceptance form after being contacted by email with the scholarship offer and instructions for acceptance.
official.application_route: Online through the GS/OAS scholarship application portal, uploading one combined PDF (max 5 MB) with all supporting documents.
official.study_mode: 100% online via Canvas; at least 4.5 hours per week over one semester of synchronous (live) and asynchronous content
official.citizenship_residency: Be a citizen or permanent resident of an OAS member state, except Chile.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - applicants from any active OAS member state other than Chile are eligible; Chilean nationals are excluded.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Strong interest in innovation and entrepreneurship with a strong background in business management; business concepts closely linked to climate or environmental resilience (SDG 13) or addressing a market need are especially encouraged.
official.research_requirement: No research proposal; a one-paragraph Business Concept Statement describing an innovative, resilience-building business concept that addresses an identified problem or market need.
official.description: The General Secretariat of the Organization of American States (GS/OAS) and the Universidad del Desarrollo in Chile have decided to support outstanding individuals from the Americas by awarding scholarships to pursue a certificate in Global Innovation and Entrepreneurship (dLab Global). The overriding theme is sustainability/climate change and how innovation can be used to reduce its effects, focusing on SDG 13; the course runs online through UDD's Canvas platform and successful students receive a formal certificate issued by the Universidad del Desarrollo.
official.region: Latin America and the Caribbean (the Americas)
official.program_type: PAEC (Partnership Program for Education and Training) - online certificate scholarship
official.english_requirement: Applicants whose native language is not English must submit one of: an official transcript confirming completion of studies at an English-speaking university or college within the past five years; TOEFL 570 or higher (paper-based), 230 or higher (computer-based) or 79 or higher (internet-based/IBT); or an IELTS score of 6.5 or equivalent.

source_citations: https://www.oas.org/en/scholarships/PAEC/2026/2026-2027 OAS - The UDD Scholarship Program Announcement.pdf
not_confirmed: Living cost, travel or insurance support - the announcement does not address them at all; it only lists expenses not covered
Number of scholarships available - the announcement does not state how many awards are offered
How the USD 3,400 contribution is split between the GS/OAS and the University
verification.notes: USD 3,400 / USD 3,800 / USD 400 figures, the 31 January 2027 deadline, the 16 March - 22 June 2027 course dates, the document list, selection criteria and the not-eligible categories were read directly from the OAS announcement PDF and the GS/OAS application page; the OAS Scholarships index confirms the call is currently listed as open.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a fee discount, not a living award: USD 3,400 of the USD 3,800 dLab Global course fee is paid and you must find USD 400 yourself, plus study materials, equipment and internet. Treat it as an affordable route to a UDD certificate and to Chilean innovation-ecosystem contacts rather than as income. You also need to be free for live online sessions between March and June 2027 and able to write a credible one-paragraph climate-resilience business concept in English.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career professionals from OAS member states other than Chile, with a business management background and an existing climate or market-led business idea, who can fund USD 400 and about 4.5 hours a week of live online study.
application_readiness_checklist: Draft the Business Concept Statement first - it is the document the committee scores on, and it must be one paragraph on an innovative, climate or environmentally resilient business idea addressing a market need.
Check the exclusions early: current OAS scholarship recipients, GS/OAS staff, their immediate families and GS/OAS consultants are barred.
If English is not your native language, line up a transcript from the last five years or a TOEFL/IELTS certificate now - only those three routes are accepted.
Prepare one combined PDF under 5 MB in English (or with official translations), because the portal allows exactly one upload.
Arrange a proof-of-funds document for the USD 400 balance - a bank statement or official bank letter is usually the fastest acceptable route.
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete documentation - the announcement states applications with incomplete documentation will not be accepted.
Uploading several files, or a PDF over 5 MB, when the system permits only one document upload.
Documents in another language without an official English translation.
Failing to evidence the USD 400 balance with one of the four accepted proofs.
Assuming a Chilean passport qualifies - Chile is explicitly excluded from this award.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: USD 400 of the course fee, study materials or equipment, internet access and any additional fees not included in the OAS-UDD offer; there is no living stipend, travel or insurance support.
document_audit: One PDF, maximum 5 MB, one upload only - merge everything before starting the form.
ID (passport bio page or national ID), CV, Business Concept Statement, English proof (if applicable) and proof of funds for USD 400 - nothing else is requested.
English proof only counts if the English-language study was completed within the past five years.
alerts: Deadline is 31 January 2027 but the course starts 16 March 2027, so the offer, acceptance form and Canvas onboarding land in a tight window - monitor the email address you register with.
Only selected applicants are contacted; unsuccessful applicants are not, so do not wait for a rejection.
Declining after the programme start date without proof of force majeure can trigger repayment of all funds awarded.
The GS/OAS reserves the right to cancel this scholarship announcement at any time during the process.
The course mixes synchronous (live) and asynchronous content, so your time zone matters far more than for a self-paced MOOC.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online form on the GS/OAS portal with a single combined PDF upload, an optional English interview for pre-selected candidates, then an emailed offer and a formal OAS acceptance form.

official.deadline_central_display: 15 October 2026, 5:00 p.m. Colombia time (extended closing of the Colombian focal point, ICETEX)
official.deadline_note: Focal-point deadlines differ by country and this one moved: the initial ICETEX closing was 9 October 2026, 1:00 p.m. Colombia time and was extended to 15 October 2026, 5:00 p.m. AGCID's own deadline for focal points to load preselected applications into its Platform is 30 October 2026, 23:59 Chile time; applicants in other countries must verify the deadline of their own focal point (Anexo 3).
official.application_cycle: Convocatoria del Programa de Becas de Cooperacion Sur-Sur - Republica de Chile, ano academico 2027; studies start between 1 March and 30 September 2027; National Scholarship Commission 26 October 2026; definitive results from the second half of November 2026
official.status_note: ICETEX lists the call as 'Abierta' with the Comision nacional de becas on 26 October 2026 and an extended closing of 15 October 2026, and the AGCID public call listing still shows the call live with a final application deadline of 30-10-2026; the AGCID results page has not yet published the 2027 selection (the 2026 selection is the most recent posted).
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: 'Pago del costo de arancel, matricula y costos de titulacion que cobre la respectiva institucion de educacion superior, por el tiempo que dure el programa de postgrado, con un tope de cuatro semestres academicos, o seis trimestres academicos' - payment of the tuition fee, enrolment and graduation costs charged by the respective higher-education institution, for the duration of the postgraduate programme, capped at four academic semesters or six quarters.
benefits: Pago del costo de arancel, matricula y costos de titulacion que cobre la respectiva institucion de educacion superior, por el tiempo que dure el programa de postgrado, con un tope de cuatro semestres academicos o seis trimestres academicos.

Asignacion mensual de manutencion de seiscientos mil pesos chilenos (CLP $600.000), durante el periodo de estudios, por un maximo de veinticuatro (24) meses, unicamente para programas presenciales o hibridos con permanencia en Chile.
Seguro de vida, salud y accidentes durante la vigencia de la beca, aplicable unicamente para personas becarias que desarrollen sus estudios en Chile.
Asignacion unica de noventa mil pesos chilenos (CLP $90.000) para textos y materiales de estudio durante el primer periodo academico, aplicable unicamente para programas desarrollados en Chile.

Asignacion unica de trescientos mil pesos chilenos (CLP $300.000) para apoyo a gastos de tesis o trabajo de grado, siempre que la persona becaria cumpla las condiciones academicas establecidas por AGCID.
Prioridad para programas de magister en areas estrategicas definidas por el Gobierno de Chile.
eligibility: Nationals of Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Cuba, Ecuador, Mexico, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Panama, the Dominican Republic and the CARICOM member states (Antigua and Barbuda, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Jamaica, Montserrat, Saint Lucia, St. Kitts and Nevis, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago).

Undergraduate professional degree issued by a recognised higher-education institution, with a cumulative undergraduate GPA of at least 4.0/5.0 evidenced by an official transcript issued and signed by the institution.
Unconditional (definitive) admission to an accredited Chilean master's programme listed in Anexo 1 of the call; the admission and its costs are the applicant's own responsibility.
Resident in the country of origin at the time of application and obliged to return there after completing the programme; candidates holding a residence and/or work visa in Chile are not accepted.

Preferably at least twelve (12) months of professional experience acquired after the undergraduate degree and related to the master's programme applied for; public officials and academic, teaching or research staff of officially recognised higher-education institutions are prioritised.

Over 20 and under 65 years of age at the closing date of the call (as published by the Colombian focal point); AGCID scholarships are incompatible with any other scholarship for study in Chile, and the spouse of a current AGCID scholarship holder in the same call cannot be awarded a scholarship.
requirements: Apply through the national focal point: AGCID evaluates only applications officially submitted by the focal point, and applications sent directly by applicants are not considered.
Submit ANEXO 4 - Formulario de Solicitud de Beca AGCID, completed on a computer and signed, using the unmodified official layout.
Submit ANEXO 5 - Declaracion de Salud y Enfermedades Preexistentes, completed and signed by a licensed physician.
Upload all documents as legible PDFs in Spanish; documents that are not legible, are in another language, contain a password or display errors are discarded and not taken into account.
Reach a minimum of 55 base points in the preselection scoring in order to be considered at all.

Dedicate yourself exclusively to the funded study programme, comply with the academic regime of the Chilean institution and the obligations set by AGCID, including submitting the approved thesis at the end of the studies.
documents: ANEXO 4 - Formulario de Solicitud de Beca AGCID, completed on a computer and signed in the official layout.

Carta de aceptacion definitiva del programa de magister, on university letterhead, stating unconditional acceptance, the delivery mode, start and end dates including the thesis and degree exam, and the matricula and annual arancel values.
ANEXO 5 - Declaracion de Salud y Enfermedades Preexistentes, completed and signed by a licensed physician.

Undergraduate degree certificate and official undergraduate transcript showing the weighted cumulative average, issued and signed by the institution; foreign documents require an official Spanish translation and foreign transcripts must state the 1 to 5 grading scale.

Socioeconomic evidence: a copy of a domestic public-utility bill (electricity, gas or water) issued within the last 60 working days showing the estrato and address, plus the SISBEN IV classification updated for 2025 where the applicant has one.

Profile pack: updated CV, a dated and signed motivation letter in Spanish of one to two pages and at least 500 words, a one-page preliminary thesis proposal, one academic reference letter (relatives not accepted), an employer sponsorship letter where applicable, the AGCID information format for the master's programme and the scholar, and a legible copy of the national identity card on both sides.
selection_criteria: ICETEX preselection, scored out of 100 base points: related professional experience 40% (more than 85 months 40 pts; 61-84 months 35; 37-60 months 30; 12-36 months 25).
Academic average 40% (4.6-5.0 = 40 pts; 4.3-4.5 = 30; 4.0-4.2 = 20), evaluated only on the weighted cumulative average in the official transcript, without rounding.
Socioeconomic factor 20%: SISBEN IV categories A1-B7 = 20 pts, C1-C18 = 18, D1-D3 = 16, D4-D21 = 14; where no SISBEN IV is available, estratos 1-2 = 12 pts, 3-4 = 10, 5-6 = 8.

Up to 10 non-cumulative bonus points for serving as a public official or as academic, teaching or research staff of a recognised higher-education institution; for a master's in an area prioritised by the Government of Chile; for membership of an ethnic community recognised by the Ministry of the Interior; for RUV certification as a victim of the armed conflict; or for having been a beneficiary of an ICETEX credit or administered fund. A minimum of 55 base points is required.
Tiebreakers, in order: highest academic average, then preference for women as recorded on the identity card, then the earliest completed submission.

Final AGCID Selection Committee scoring: priority assigned by the country 20%, alignment with Chile's foreign-policy priorities 15%, professional experience 25%, employing institution (public 100 / private 50 points) 10%, gender 10%, age 5%, and applying to a university in the regions rather than the Metropolitan Region 5%; the decision is definitive and unappealable.
coverage: 100% of the matricula, arancel and titulation costs charged by the Chilean higher-education institution, for a maximum of four academic semesters or six quarters.
Monthly maintenance allowance of CLP 600,000 for up to 24 months, only for programmes delivered in person or hybrid with presence in Chile.
Life, health and accident insurance for the duration of the scholarship, only for scholars studying in Chile.
One-time allocation of CLP 90,000 for texts and study materials in the first academic period, only for programmes delivered in Chile.

One-time allocation of CLP 300,000 for thesis or final-degree project costs, subject to AGCID's academic conditions (a grade average equal to or above 5.5, evidenced before the nineteenth month in which AGCID pays the monthly allowance).
application_method: Secure unconditional admission to a Chilean master's programme listed in Anexo 1, at your own cost, before applying.
Complete and sign ANEXO 4 on a computer in the official layout, and have ANEXO 5 signed by a licensed physician.

Upload every required document as a legible Spanish PDF on the postulation platform of your focal point (for Colombia, the ICETEX platform); documents sent by post, by email or at ICETEX service points are not accepted.

National Scholarship Commission (CNB) preselection on 26 October 2026; the focal point forwards its ranked list to AGCID - each focal point may submit a maximum of ten prioritized preselected candidates.

AGCID's Selection Committee makes the final, definitive and unappealable decision; definitive results are communicated from the second half of November 2026 through the 'Resultados de Postulacion' section of the AGCID website.
The award is formalised by signing the AGCID scholarship acceptance document (ANEXO 2).
official.application_route: Online through your country's AGCID focal point (for Colombia, the ICETEX postulation platform); applications sent directly to AGCID are not considered.
official.study_mode: In-person, hybrid or online as stated in the definitive acceptance letter; the monthly maintenance allowance, the insurance and the study-materials allowance do not apply to programmes delivered virtually.
official.citizenship_residency: Nationals of the listed Latin American and Caribbean countries, resident in their country of origin; applicants holding a Chilean residence and/or work visa are not accepted, and selected scholars must return to their country of origin after the programme.
official.international_eligibility: Yes for nationals of the listed countries - the programme exists to bring Latin American and Caribbean professionals to study in Chile; Chileans are not part of this call.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The master's programme must appear in Anexo 1 - Listado de Programas de Magister Acreditados; priority is given to Chile's strategic areas (astronomy, mining, Antarctic sciences, renewable energies, marine resources, economic development, international trade, international relations, sovereignty, territorial integrity and national security, and the fight against organised crime and terrorism) and to public officials and academic, teaching or research staff of recognised higher-education institutions.
official.research_requirement: A brief description, of about one page, of the possible area and topic of the final thesis; the thesis support allocation additionally requires an approved thesis project, a schedule signed by the thesis supervisor and a certificate of academic performance.
official.duration: Up to 24 months (maximum four academic semesters or six quarters), according to the official duration of the chosen master's programme.
official.description: The Agencia Chilena de Cooperacion Internacional para el Desarrollo (AGCID), within its Programa de Becas de Cooperacion Sur-Sur, offers from academic year 2027 scholarships to carry out master's studies at Chilean universities or other higher-education institutions. The purpose of the programme is to contribute to the formation of advanced human capital through the participation of Latin American and Caribbean professionals in master's programmes taught by Chilean higher-education institutions accredited with a high level of excellence.

not_confirmed: English language requirement - not published; the call is delivered in Spanish and AGCID requests an official document issued by the embassy of the applicant's country certifying command of the Spanish language, where applicable for that country
Exact number of scholarships for Colombia - the call sets no fixed number of scholarships per country; each focal point may submit at most ten prioritized preselected candidates
Age limits in the AGCID call document itself - the 20-65 range is published by the Colombian focal point (ICETEX), not in the AGCID convocatoria PDF
verification.notes: CLP 600,000 per month, CLP 90,000, CLP 300,000 and the 100% matricula/arancel/titulacion coverage were read from the AGCID-hosted 2027 call document and confirmed on the ICETEX focal-point page; the AGCID public call listing shows the call live with a 30-10-2026 closing for focal points, while ICETEX extended its own closing to 15 October 2026, 5:00 p.m. Colombia time.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a genuine full-cost master's award - tuition, enrolment, graduation, a CLP 600,000 monthly stipend and health insurance - but only if you already hold admission to a programme on AGCID's Anexo 1 list, and only if that programme runs in person or hybrid in Chile. Air fares, the visa, university admission fees and personal spending remain yours to fund, and you commit to returning to your home country afterwards. Because each focal point can only send ten prioritized candidates, your national ranking matters as much as the quality of your file.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career public-sector officials and university lecturers from the listed Latin American and Caribbean countries who already hold unconditional admission to an accredited Chilean master's, can evidence a strong undergraduate average, a low socioeconomic score and a long related work history.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your exact programme appears in Anexo 1 on the AGCID site before spending anything on admission - programmes outside the list are not considered at all.

Secure the unconditional acceptance letter early: it must state the modality, start and end dates including the thesis and degree exam, and the matricula and annual arancel values, on university letterhead.

Download ANEXO 4, ANEXO 5 and the master's-programme-and-scholar information format from AGCID's Ofertas Vigentes, and type ANEXO 4 on a computer - any change to the official layout excludes the application.
Book the physician who will sign ANEXO 5 in good time, and request your official transcript showing the weighted cumulative average (minimum 4.0/5.0), issued and signed by the university.
Refresh your socioeconomic evidence: a public-utility bill issued within the last 60 working days showing estrato and address, plus a SISBEN IV category updated in 2025.
Write the motivation letter in Spanish (one to two pages, at least 500 words) plus a one-page preliminary thesis proposal, and line up an academic referee who is not a relative.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a programme that is not on Anexo 1, or choosing a virtual programme while expecting the stipend, insurance and study-materials allowance, which do not apply online.
Altering, completing by hand or leaving unsigned the ANEXO 4 or ANEXO 5 official formats, or submitting them without the physician's signature.
Illegible, password-protected or non-Spanish PDFs, which are discarded rather than queried.
A transcript without the weighted cumulative average, or a foreign transcript that does not state the 1 to 5 grading scale.
A current-employment certificate older than 30 calendar days at closing, or a utility bill older than 60 working days.
Being in arrears with an ICETEX credit line - this is checked in ICETEX systems and automatically disqualifies the candidate.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: University admission and application costs, visa and migration procedures, air fares and transfers, travel insurance, taxes, personal expenses and any costs for family members or companions - AGCID finances none of these.
document_audit: Every document must be a legible Spanish PDF with no password; the acceptance letter must carry the university's letterhead and seal.
Foreign degrees and certificates need an official Spanish translation, and foreign transcripts must state the minimum and maximum passing grades on a 1 to 5 scale.

Experience certificates must name the employer, dates of service and functions; the current-employment certificate must be no more than 30 calendar days old at closing, and self-sworn statements are never accepted.
Socioeconomic scoring is documentary: SISBEN IV updated for 2025 if you have it, otherwise the estrato printed on the utility bill.
alerts: Focal-point deadlines move: ICETEX first closed on 9 October 2026 at 1:00 p.m. Colombia time and extended it to 15 October 2026 at 5:00 p.m., while AGCID gives focal points until 30 October 2026, 23:59 Chile time - confirm the live date with your own focal point.
Admission and funding are separate steps: you must already hold the unconditional acceptance and pay all admission costs yourself before you can apply.

Preselection is not selection - the focal point ranks candidates and ICETEX forwards at most ten per country to AGCID, whose committee's decision is final and unappealable, so your position in the national ranking matters as much as your file.
Only selected candidates are notified, with definitive results published from the second half of November 2026 on the AGCID results page; keep the email address you register under constant watch.
Choosing an online programme quietly removes the stipend, the insurance and the study-materials allowance, leaving only tuition coverage.
Early termination of the scholarship for cause obliges you to repay all amounts paid except the insurance, and bars reapplying for an AGCID scholarship.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You assemble and submit the file on your focal point's platform, the focal point pre-selects and ranks candidates (for Colombia, the ICETEX platform and the 26 October 2026 National Scholarship Commission), then the AGCID Selection Committee makes the final award from the second half of November 2026.
